neighbours.label: the comma (or ' either') after a verb or participle that opens an inserted qualifier of manner or extent, where 'directly or indirectly' / 'in whole or in part' is expected (legal style: "…may not be used, [either] wholly or partly, …"); not list commas, and not 'either' choosing between nouns
fire: This manual may not be reproduced, either wholly or in part, without the publisher's consent.
The seller is not responsible for any damage arising, directly or indirectly, from misuse of the product.
All of these artists were influenced, either consciously or unconsciously, by the Dutch masters.
The licensed material may not be resold, in whole or in part, to any third party.
No employee may benefit, directly or indirectly, from contracts awarded by the council.
Most of the houses in the valley were destroyed, either partly or completely, by the flood.
A person is treated as resident if he can be reached, by post or otherwise, at an address in the state.
The prize fund is financed, either fully or partially, by private donors.
quiet: This manual, the software and the cables may not be returned without the publisher's consent.
The seller, the carrier and the insurer are not responsible for misuse of the product.
In those years, all of these artists studied the Dutch masters in Amsterdam.
The licensed material includes photographs, maps, drawings and sound recordings.
However, no employee may accept gifts from contractors working for the council.
You can choose either the house in the valley or the flat in town.
A person who lives in the state, works there and pays tax there is treated as resident.
The prize fund, which was set up in 1990, is managed by private donors.

notes: Card: peaks on ',' or ' either' right before 'directly or indirectly', 'fully or in part', 'totally or in part'; output promotes 'either', 'whether', 'directly'. Probes: 'copied, either wholly or partly' 0.49, 'caused, directly or indirectly' 0.44, but also 'caused, however large,' 0.44, so the pole reads the slot (comma after the participle), not the words that follow. 'pay either by card' 0.07, list commas 0.01. Near misses keep legal style with commas in lists, after nouns and after openers.
